hero.h1:
Fly a little closer.
Meet the WUDFLY Spectre.
hero.lede: Skim the scenery. Bank into the next gap. Discover the joy of a small wing with a quick response in Nanawing's recreation of the WUDFLY Spectre. Then try three more wings, each with its own pace and feel. All four are free to fly in your browser.

compare.h2: Four wings. Find your kind of flying.
compare.note: Performance measured in Nanawing, not real-world aircraft specifications. Stall speed is wings-level and unpowered; banked turns need more. Battery is the simulated pack and its full-throttle current.

paragraphs: Your first wing doesn't have to be one you outgrow. Learn to hold a line, link your turns and bring a lap together in Nanawing's own flying wing. The lowest stall speed in the hangar and a quick roll make the One a welcoming place to start.
When you're ready, open the throttle. A measured 191 km/h in the simulator leaves plenty of room to grow. Pick a course, set a time, then come back for one cleaner lap.

Know the course? Now feel it at a different pace. The Morok takes you up to a measured 249 km/h in Nanawing, turning a familiar lap into a fresh challenge. Look ahead, choose your line and let one turn lead into the next.
Its slower roll and higher stall speed than the One reward a little more planning. Try the same course in both: the gates haven't moved, but the way you approach them will.

For the moment you want everything to arrive faster. At a measured 323 km/h in Nanawing, the Sukhoi is the fastest wing in the hangar, with the strongest climb to match. Open it up and watch the scenery rush past.
That speed asks something of you. The highest stall speed and slowest roll of the four mean you'll need to plan your banks and commit to your line. Find the rhythm, and every clean gate feels earned.

Small wing. Quick turns. A new reason to take the scenic route. Our recreation of WUDFLY's 600 mm, 215 g twin-motor wing pairs the lowest top speed in the hangar with the quickest roll. Its measured 100 km/h top speed gives you more time to read the scenery; its crisp bank response invites you to get closer.

Bring a controller and discover its party trick: differential thrust. The yaw stick varies the two motors' speeds to swing the nose, giving the Spectre a move no other wing in the hangar has. It works best at lower speeds and needs more than 10% throttle. A keyboard still handles pitch, roll and throttle; yaw needs a controller.
spectre.note: Our simulator model is an original recreation of WUDFLY's design, built from public product photos. Its handling is a simulator approximation, not a manufacturer-validated flight model.

wudfly.h3: Love the flight? Meet the real wing.
paragraphs: The Spectre starts with WUDFLY: a designer of 3D-printable RC planes and FPV wings. Watch the real aircraft fly, explore the build, or visit WUDFLY for the STL files, build guides and INAV setups to make your own.

paragraphs: A test bot flies each aircraft on the same flight model you play with. A settled full-throttle level run gives top speed, a full-stick roll gives roll rate, and a 20° full-power climb gives climb rate.

Stall speed is the unpowered, wings-level 1 g lift limit from each wing's aerodynamic curve. The in-game stall warning comes earlier, at 27, 32, 39 and 31 km/h for the One, Morok, Sukhoi and Spectre, and banked turns need more speed. The bench is rerun after any tuning, so these numbers match what you fly.

faq.q: Which Nanawing aircraft should I fly first?
faq.a: Try the Spectre for a slower pace and quick banks close to the scenery. Brand new to flying? The Nanawing One is a welcoming starting point, with the lowest stall speed in the hangar. Choose the Morok for more speed, or the Sukhoi for the fastest flight of the four.

faq.q: Is the WUDFLY Spectre in Nanawing the real aircraft?
faq.a: It's our recreation of WUDFLY's design, with the real wing's 600 mm span, twin motors and white-and-yellow livery. Its handling is a simulator approximation. The real Spectre is designed and sold by WUDFLY at wudfly.com.

faq.q: Can every aircraft race every course?
faq.a: Yes. Each of the four courses keeps a separate board for each aircraft, so you race pilots in the same plane. Only your best lap counts.
No. All four fly on a keyboard, and a gamepad or a USB RC radio works too. The Spectre's yaw needs a controller's yaw stick.

final.h2: Your next favourite wing is one flight away.
final.lede: Start with the Spectre. Stay for one more lap. Fly all four free on your laptop or desktop, right in your browser. No install. No login.
